settings.name_in_paper: Treatment recommendation with distributional targets (general feasible set M_K)
unmapped: Objective is a distributional functional T of the outcome cdf (inequality, welfare, poverty measures), not the mean; T is Lipschitz w.r.t. sup-norm on cdfs with constant C (Assumption 2.3)

Recommendation is a mixture weight vector delta in a closed feasible subset M_K of the simplex (possibly with capacity/similarity constraints); regret is max_{delta in M_K} T(<delta,F>) - T(<recommended delta,F>)
Outcomes are supported on a known interval [a,b] with cdfs in a known convex class D; arbitrary dependence across arm components of the potential outcome vector
Sequential elimination policies use the Lipschitz constant C of the functional in their threshold; the learner knows the functional T and the class D
settings.definition_quote: The objective is to use the outcomes of the~$n$ subjects observed to give a recommendation~$\pi_{n,n+1}$ in~$\mathscr{M}_K$ ... r_n(\pi, \mathscr{M}_K) := \max_{\delta \in \mathscr{M}_K} \mathsf{T}(\langle \delta, \mathbf{F} \rangle) - \mathsf{T}(\langle \pi_{n,n+1}(Z_n, G_{n+1}), \mathbf{F} \rangle ).

settings.name_in_paper: Treatment recommendation with incompatibility constraints (M_K as in Example 2.6)
unmapped: Objective is a distributional functional T of the outcome cdf, Lipschitz w.r.t. sup-norm with constant C
Recommendation is a mixture weight vector in M_K = union over a partition A_1..A_m of subsets of the face simplices (incompatibility constraints)
Outcomes supported on known [a,b] with cdfs in a known convex class D
The learner knows the Lipschitz constant C (used in the elimination threshold) and the functional T
settings.definition_quote: Let~$m$ be an integer such that~$1 < m \leq K$, let~$\{A_1, \hdots, A_m\}$ be a partition of~$\mathcal{I}$ (i.e., the incompatible groups of treatments), and set \mathscr{M}_K = \bigcup_{j = 1}^m \mathscr{M}_{A_j, K}

settings.name_in_paper: Treatment recommendation with distributional targets (lower bound)
unmapped: Objective is a distributional functional T of the outcome cdf, Lipschitz w.r.t. sup-norm and varying at least linearly along a segment J_tau of cdfs in D (Assumption 3.1)
Recommendation is a mixture weight vector in a closed feasible set M_K of the simplex with at least two elements
Outcomes supported on known [a,b]; learner knows the functional, the class D and the feasible set
settings.definition_quote: for every policy~$\pi$ with recommendations in~$\mathscr{M}_K$, and any randomization measure~$\P_G$ ... where the supremum is taken over all potential outcome vectors with independent marginals and cdfs in~$\{J_{\tau}:\tau \in [0,1]\}$.

symbols.diam_M: Euclidean diameter of the feasible set of mixture weights M_K

conditions: supremum over outcome vectors with independent marginals and cdfs in the segment {J_tau}

source.label: thm:lbn
source.quote: Then there exists a constant~$c > 0$, independent of~$K$,~$n$ and~$\mathscr{M}_K$, such that for every policy~$\pi$ with recommendations in~$\mathscr{M}_K$, and any randomization measure~$\P_G$, it holds that \sup_{F^1, \hdots, F^K \in \{J_{\tau}:\tau \in [0,1]\}} \mathbb{E}[r_n(\pi, {\mathscr{M}_K})] \geq c \times \mathrm{diam}^2(\mathscr{M}_K)/ \sqrt{n}, for every n \geq K

results.notes: Paper's n is T. Constant c independent of K, n, M_K.

symbols.kappa_M: structural spread constant kappa(M_K) of the feasible set; >= 1/272 * max ||delta||^2 * min_j (range of delta_j)^3 and >= (min_j max delta_j - 1/2)_+^2 (so >= 1/4 when M_K contains all vertices)

conditions: supremum over outcome vectors with independent marginals and cdfs in {J_tau}

source.label: Thm: UniformLowermixed
source.quote: \sup_{F^1, \hdots, F^K \in \{J_{\tau}:\tau \in [0,1]\}} \mathbb{E}[r_n(\pi, {\mathscr{M}_K})] \geq c  \kappa(\mathscr{M}_K) \sqrt{K/n}, ~~\text{ for every } n \geq K ... Furthermore, \kappa(\mathscr{M}_K) \geq  \frac{1}{272} \times \max_{\delta \in \mathscr{M}_K} \|\delta\|^2 \times \min_{j = 1}^K (\max_{\delta \in \mathscr{M}_K} \delta_j - \min_{\delta \in \mathscr{M}_K} \delta_j)^3

results.notes: When M_K contains E_K, kappa >= 1/4, giving Omega(sqrt(K/n)).

symbols.kappa_H: kappa(H, M_K) for a partition H of the treatments (bound is max over partitions)
symbols.H_size: number of blocks |H| of the partition

conditions: supremum over outcome vectors with independent marginals and cdfs in {J_tau}

source.label: prop: UniformLowermixed
source.quote: \sup_{F^1, \hdots, F^K \in \{J_{\tau}:\tau \in [0,1]\}} \mathbb{E}[r_n(\pi, {\mathscr{M}_K})] \geq c \max_{\mathcal{H} \in \{ \text{Partitions of } \{1, \hdots, K\} \}}\kappa(\mathcal{H}, \mathscr{M}_K) \sqrt{|\mathcal{H}|/n}, ~~\forall n \geq K

results.notes: General lower bound in the appendix from which Theorems 3.2 and 3.3 follow; max over partitions represented by declared symbols.

symbols.eps_n: worst-case optimization error of the discretization M_K^n of M_K
symbols.C_T: Lipschitz constant of the functional T w.r.t. sup-norm on cdfs (Assumption 2.3)
symbols.beta_n: min_j |Pi_{n,j}|, smallest number of subjects assigned to a treatment

tuning: partition Pi_n of subjects; discretization M_K^n

source.label: thm:NMAPup
source.quote: Then the SA policy~$\hat{\pi}$ with partition~$\Pi_n$,~discretization~$\mathscr{M}_K^n$ and~$\beta_n := \min_{j = 1, \hdots, K}|\Pi_{n,j}|$ satisfies \sup_{F^i \in \mathscr{D}} \mathbb{E}\left[r_n(\hat{\pi}, \mathscr{M}_K)\right] \leq \varepsilon(n) + 3.01 \times C ~\sqrt{\log(K)/\beta_n}, \text{ for every } n \geq K.

results.notes: With balanced partitions (beta_n >= floor(n/K)) and eps(n) <= sqrt(K/n) this is O(sqrt(K log K / n)). Outcomes in [a,b] rescaled to bounded_01.

source.label: thm:FSApartition
source.quote: the SE policy~$\tilde{\pi}$ as in Policy~\ref{pol:FSE_partition} satisfies \sup \E \left[ r_n(\tilde{\pi}, \mathscr{M}_K) \right] \leq \eps(n) + 4C \sqrt{\frac{K}{n}} D_{n,K} + 4C\frac{K^{1-\frac{3\eta}{4+2\eta}} }{\sqrt{n}} \times (1+18.5\eta^{-1})^2, ~\forall n \geq 2K, where~$D_{n,K} :=  \sqrt{K\log\del[0]{17K}} \wedge  \sqrt{\log(3.01 \times K(n+2))}$.

results.notes: eta here is the policy's tuning parameter (not a learning rate). Includes M_K = E_K (Policy 2) as special case.
